packages.title: Farm Practices Survey sample-method QA
facts: The 2026 FPS metadata states questions were sent to approximately 7,000 holdings in England.
Survey estimates therefore have sampling and response uncertainty.
Reported percentages are estimates for the survey population.
Sampling uncertainty prevents false parcel-level certainty.
No individual holding is inferred from aggregate percentages.

packages.title: Nutrient-management-plan 69% QA
facts: In 2026, 69% of farmers in the FPS had a nutrient management plan.
This is a proportion of surveyed holdings, not a GHG reduction rate.
Plan existence does not quantify emissions.
Comparison with earlier years must preserve survey design.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Nutrient-management plan versus GHG QA
facts: Effective nutrient management can help minimise GHG emissions and diffuse pollution.
The survey measures practices such as nutrient plans and soil monitoring.
Practice adoption is not direct emissions measurement.
Potential environmental benefit is not observed CO2e reduction.
No reduction factor is invented.

packages.title: Anaerobic-digestion 15% QA
facts: The 2026 FPS reports 15% of farmers processing waste, crops or feedstocks by anaerobic digestion.
The comparable 2022 figure shown is 8%.
This percentage is adoption activity, not energy generation or GHG savings.
Survey adoption does not identify plant scale.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Anaerobic-digestion material mix QA
facts: The FPS reports crops including silage as the most common AD material type at 7% of farmers in 2026.
Slurries and manures were reported by 6%.
Material categories are survey responses and can overlap with feedstock questions.
Feedstock prevalence does not measure methane capture.
No parcel methane value is inferred.

packages.title: Farm GHG-action 47% QA
facts: The 2026 FPS introduction reports 47% of farmers currently taking action to reduce farm GHG emissions.
That figure is self-reported action adoption.
It is not a measured percentage reduction in GHG emissions.
Action prevalence cannot be multiplied by inventory totals without a method.
No parcel result is created.

packages.title: Farm emissions action-types QA
facts: Among farms taking action, reported measures include recycling, energy efficiency, reduced tillage and improved nitrogen application accuracy.
Action categories describe practices rather than tonnes of CO2e.
Multiple actions can be reported by the same holding.
Percentages cannot be summed as mutually exclusive shares.
No emissions savings are invented.

packages.title: Methane-suppressing feed 2% QA
facts: The 2026 FPS emissions section reports 2% of farms regularly using methane-suppressing feed products.
This is a practice-adoption statistic.
It does not report measured methane reduction at those farms.
Livestock type and dosage are not supplied as parcel-level evidence.
No methane reduction factor is inferred.

packages.title: Manure/fertiliser spreading activity QA
facts: The 2026 FPS introduction reports 79% of holdings spread manure or slurry on grass or arable land.
It also reports 82% spread fertiliser on grass and arable land.
Spreading prevalence is activity, not nitrogen mass or emissions.
Farmer/contractor delivery categories must remain distinct.
No parcel GHG is inferred.

packages.title: Spreader farmer-versus-contractor QA
facts: The spreader survey separates farmer-only, mixed farmer/contractor and contractor-only activity.
Operator mode is not an emissions factor.
Percentages are holding-level survey responses.
Changing contractor shares do not directly quantify emissions changes.
No parcel estimate is produced.

packages.title: Solid-manure uncovered-storage QA
facts: In 2026, 60% of livestock holdings reported facility to store solid manure in the open on a field site without cover.
Multiple storage types could be selected.
Facility availability is not the same as the location where all manure is stored.
Storage type can affect environmental risk but is not direct GHG measurement.
No parcel methane or N2O value is inferred.

packages.title: Slurry above-ground uncovered-storage QA
facts: In 2026, 46% of holdings with slurry storage reported above-ground tanks without cover.
The survey also reports other lagoon and below-ground storage categories.
Storage prevalence does not quantify slurry volume.
Uncovered storage does not itself provide an emissions measurement.
No parcel methane value is inferred.

packages.title: Manure/slurry upgrade-plan QA
facts: The 2026 FPS reports 19% of holdings planning to enlarge, upgrade or reconstruct manure or slurry storage.
Of those planning changes, most expected changes within three years.
Future upgrade intention is not completed infrastructure.
Planned change is not observed emissions reduction.
No future benefit is recorded as current.

packages.title: Slurry-separator adoption QA
facts: The 2026 FPS reports 19% of farmers saying they have a slurry separator.
The comparable 2025 figure shown is 11%.
Separator adoption can affect management but does not itself quantify GHG savings.
Survey prevalence is not parcel equipment verification.
No emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Clover temporary-grassland QA
facts: The 2026 FPS reports 82% of livestock holdings sow some or all temporary grassland with a clover mix.
Clover can reduce nitrogen requirements in suitable conditions.
Practice prevalence does not equal fertiliser reduction mass.
Potential environmental effect is not measured parcel GHG.
No parcel reduction is inferred.

packages.title: High-sugar-grass QA
facts: The 2026 FPS introduction reports high-sugar grasses on 75% of livestock holdings with temporary grassland.
The practice may improve production efficiency in some situations.
Adoption does not directly quantify GHG reduction.
Livestock and field-specific conditions are not supplied.
No parcel effect is inferred.

packages.title: Livestock ration/advice QA
facts: The 2026 FPS introduction reports 68% of holdings with livestock use a ration formulation programme or nutritional advice.
This is a management-practice statistic.
Feeding advice is not direct methane measurement.
Productivity effects require additional activity data and methods.
No parcel methane value is produced.

packages.title: Livestock feeding GHG-causality guard QA
facts: Defra notes livestock feeding and breeding practices can affect productivity and GHG emissions.
Such statements describe mechanisms and potential effects.
They do not provide farm-specific measured emissions.
Causal potential must not be converted to a numerical reduction without evidence.
No parcel factor is invented.

packages.title: British Survey of Fertiliser Practice 2025 dataset QA
facts: The BSFP dataset page was updated 16 July 2026 with the 2025 time-series dataset.
BSFP reports fertiliser practices rather than direct GHG measurements.
Dataset vintage must be preserved when compared with earlier years.
Great Britain survey scope must not be confused with England-only FPS results.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: BSFP GB versus FPS England QA
facts: The fertiliser-usage collection describes BSFP as Great Britain statistics.
The February 2026 FPS applies to England.
Survey scopes must remain separate when comparing fertiliser practices.
Different survey populations can produce different rates.
No cross-geography parcel inference is made.

packages.title: Fertiliser application versus GHG QA
facts: BSFP measures fertiliser practice and application information.
Fertiliser application is activity data, not direct N2O emissions.
Emission calculation requires inventory methodology and factors.
Application statistics alone do not establish parcel GHG.
No default emission factor is silently applied.

packages.title: UK Energy in Brief future-release QA
facts: The UK Energy in Brief 2025 announcement lists a release date of 30 July 2026.
At the current 25 July 2026 date the release remains in the future.
The announcement page being updated on 18 July does not make the statistics released.
Future release metadata must not be treated as current observations.
No future values are extracted.

packages.title: CCA old/new guidance boundary QA
facts: 2026 statutory guidance applies to the new CCA scheme beginning January 2026.
Earlier guidance remains relevant to live obligations from previous phases.
Old and new scheme target periods must not be merged.
Certification periods and enforcement can overlap in calendar time.
No historical target is relabelled under the new scheme.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel inference guard QA
facts: Subnational energy, rail, programme and farm-survey sources use different units and geographies.
None of the reviewed sources alone supplies verified cadastral geometry plus parcel-level measured GHG for this slot.
Activity, survey, target, energy and estimated-emissions metrics remain semantically distinct.
Parcel binding remains a separate gate.
No parcel value is fabricated.
